explanation: Repeatedly append the smaller head node of the two sorted lists, choosing the first list on equal values. Append the remaining suffix after one list ends. A temporary dummy simplifies linking.
timeComplexity: O(m + n) time. Each merge step consumes one node; the leftover suffix is appended at once.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space; original nodes are reused. Only the dummy head and a fixed number of pointers are extra.
attribution: Unmodified reference source: epi_judge_cpp_solutions/sorted_lists_merge.cc. Elements of Programming Interviews Judge authors; repository LICENSE: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: At each step, the smaller current head is no greater than any unconsumed node in either sorted list, so appending it preserves sortedness. Advancing only the selected list preserves every other node. When one list is exhausted, the other suffix is already sorted and can be appended unchanged. Each original node is included exactly once.
walkthrough: Merge [-3, 4, 9] and [-2, 4, 10]. Choose -3, then -2. At equal heads 4 and 4, take the first list’s 4, then the other 4. Finish with 9 and the remaining 10. Return [-3, -2, 4, 4, 9, 10].
edgeCases: Either or both input lists may be null.
Duplicates are preserved rather than coalesced.
Comparing values directly avoids subtraction overflow at integer extremes.
